newsitem.title: USA: No W.House meeting before budget deal -- Sen Lott.
newsitem.headline: No W.House meeting before budget deal -- Sen Lott.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday there will be no White House meeting between President Clinton and congressional leaders until an agreement is reached on balancing the budget.
"We feel that it would be useless, and maybe counterproductive if we went down there before we have something to actually agree on," he told reporters.

The White House had pencilled in time for a possible meeting on Wednesday, but has cancelled that and saved time in the president's schedule on Friday should such a meeting materialize, administration officials said Tuesday.
Lott expressed optimism on the chances for a tax cut this year. "It looks to me like they are moving toward an agreement that could involve some tax relief," the Mississippi Republican said.
He said he still expects budget negotiations to wrap up this week.
White House and congressional negotiators resumed talks at 2:45 p.m. (1845 GMT) on the issues of defense spending and mandatory spending outside of health care and retirement programs.
